newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chinese tea consumption, output to expand.
newsitem.headline: Chinese tea consumption, output to expand.

text.p: Chinese production and consumption of different kinds of tea will expand as increasing affluence puts more money in people's pockets, the president of the China Tea Science Society said on Tuesday.
Chen Zongmao told an Asia Tea Industry conference that tea production in China should rise to 650,000 tonnes in 2000 from 588,500 tonnes in 1995.
"The demand (for) various tea products is likely to continue with increasing affluence," Chen said in a paper presented to the meeting.
While green and black tea would still form the bulk consumed in China, other varieties of tea -- instant, flavoured, decaffeinated, organically-grown, foamy, and herbal -- would gain favour, he said.

"Various foods using tea as the raw material (will be) developed, such as tea-rice, tea-noodle, tea-cake, tea-biscuits, tea-wine, tea-candy and tea-ice cream. These will promote tea consumption," Chen said.

China has the largest tea plantations in the world with up to 1.16 million hectares planted. It exported 158,000 tonnes in 1995, down from 204,500 tonnes in 1994, about half of it green tea while black tea made up 30 percent.
The tea is exported to overseas Chinese communities, Morocco, Russia, Hong Kong, Saudi Arabia, Japan, the United States, Poland, Tunisia and Libya.
